repository_card.frontier: The README records vertex-coordinate tree gauge fixing; the stronger full edge-coordinate equivalence, every face-holonomy formula and planar embedding comparison remain open.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: The maximal-tree simulation paper gives a concrete comparison target for the edge-model frontier. Dictionary: tree edges -> vertex gauge coordinates, complementary edges -> reduced physical coordinates. Preserve product Haar, root convention and boundary holonomies; algorithmic digitization does not establish the exact measure equivalence.
repository_card.next_finite_task: Write the edge map and inverse for the three-face cyclic-dual disk; count E=(V-1)+(E-V+1), derive each face word and test reconstruction before attempting the general product-Haar proof.
repository_card.falsifier: Reject the proposed map if any edge cannot be reconstructed, if a residual global gauge freedom is silently removed, or if face orientation changes the holonomy.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: Efficient Quantum Simulations of Yang-Mills theory with Maximal-tree Gauge
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: abstract and maximal-tree gauge construction
sources.source_claim: Li and collaborators use maximal-tree gauge and field-amplitude digitization to obtain polynomial resource bounds for Hamiltonian Yang-Mills simulation through QSVT.
sources.limits: Hamiltonian simulation complexity is distinct from an exact Haar edge-coordinate equivalence, Euclidean reflection positivity, and a continuum mass gap. First posted 27 August; a September news mention is not a new submission.

sources.title: Non-Abelian string melting and thermalization in an open lattice gauge theory
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: model, thermalization discussion and strong-dephasing reduction
sources.source_claim: A tensor-network study couples 1+1D SU(2) gauge theory with matter to a gauge-preserving Lindblad bath. It finds nonmonotonic relaxation and derives an exclusion-process description in a strong-dephasing limit.
sources.limits: This is an open-system finite/truncated lattice setting, not pure 4D Euclidean Yang-Mills. A Liouvillian relaxation rate is not automatically a Hamiltonian gap, and the strong-dephasing expansion has its own regime.
